deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

graceful_decommission_timeout.description: The timeout duration which allows graceful decomissioning when you change the number of worker nodes directly through a terraform apply

labels.description:
The list of the labels (key/value pairs) configured on the resource and to be applied to instances in the cluster.

				**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
				Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.

name.description: The name of the cluster, unique within the project and zone.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the cluster will exist. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

region.description: The region in which the cluster and associated nodes will be created in. Defaults to global.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

cluster_config.description: Allows you to configure various aspects of the cluster.

cluster_config.cluster_tier.description: Specifies the tier of the cluster created.

cluster_config.engine.description: Specifies the engine of the cluster created.

cluster_config.staging_bucket.description: The Cloud Storage staging bucket used to stage files, such as Hadoop jars, between client machines and the cluster. Note: If you don't explicitly specify a staging_bucket then GCP will auto create / assign one for you. However, you are not guaranteed an auto generated bucket which is solely dedicated to your cluster; it may be shared with other clusters in the same region/zone also choosing to use the auto generation option.

cluster_config.temp_bucket.description: The Cloud Storage temp bucket used to store ephemeral cluster and jobs data, such as Spark and MapReduce history files. Note: If you don't explicitly specify a temp_bucket then GCP will auto create / assign one for you.

cluster_config.autoscaling_config.description: The autoscaling policy config associated with the cluster.

cluster_config.autoscaling_config.policy.description: The autoscaling policy used by the cluster.

cluster_config.auxiliary_node_groups.nod.description: The node group instance group configuration.
The name of a Google Compute Engine machine type to create for the master
The name of a minimum generation of CPU family for the auxiliary node group. If not specified, GCP will default to a predetermined computed value for each zone.
Specifies the number of auxiliary nodes to create. If not specified, GCP will default to a predetermined computed value.
The Compute Engine accelerator (GPU) configuration for these instances. Can be specified multiple times.
The number of the accelerator cards of this type exposed to this instance. Often restricted to one of 1, 2, 4, or 8.
The short name of the accelerator type to expose to this instance. For example, nvidia-tesla-k80.
Indicates how many IOPS to provision for the disk. This sets the number of I/O operations per second that the disk can handle.
Indicates how much throughput to provision for the disk. This sets the number of throughput mb per second that the disk can handle.

Size of the primary disk attached to each node, specified in GB. The primary disk contains the boot volume and system libraries, and the smallest allowed disk size is 10GB. GCP will default to a predetermined computed value if not set (currently 500GB). Note: If SSDs are not attached, it also contains the HDFS data blocks and Hadoop working directories.
The disk type of the primary disk attached to each node. Such as "pd-ssd" or "pd-standard". Defaults to "pd-standard".
Interface type of local SSDs (default is "scsi"). Valid values: "scsi" (Small Computer System Interface), "nvme" (Non-Volatile Memory Express).
The amount of local SSD disks that will be attached to each master cluster node. Defaults to 0.

cluster_config.dataproc_metric_config.me.description: Specify one or more [available OSS metrics] (https://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/guides/monitoring#available_oss_metrics) to collect.
A source for the collection of Dataproc OSS metrics (see [available OSS metrics] (https://cloud.google.com//dataproc/docs/guides/monitoring#available_oss_metrics)).

cluster_config.encryption_config.description: The Customer managed encryption keys settings for the cluster.

cluster_config.encryption_config.kms_key.description: The Cloud KMS key name to use for PD disk encryption for all instances in the cluster.

cluster_config.endpoint_config.description: The config settings for port access on the cluster. Structure defined below.

cluster_config.endpoint_config.enable_ht.description: The flag to enable http access to specific ports on the cluster from external sources (aka Component Gateway). Defaults to false.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.description: Common config settings for resources of Google Compute Engine cluster instances, applicable to all instances in the cluster.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.intern.description: By default, clusters are not restricted to internal IP addresses, and will have ephemeral external IP addresses assigned to each instance. If set to true, all instances in the cluster will only have internal IP addresses. Note: Private Google Access (also known as privateIpGoogleAccess) must be enabled on the subnetwork that the cluster will be launched in.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.metada.description: A map of the Compute Engine metadata entries to add to all instances

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.networ.description: The name or self_link of the Google Compute Engine network to the cluster will be part of. Conflicts with subnetwork. If neither is specified, this defaults to the "default" network.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.resour.description: A map of resource manager tags to add to all instances. Keys must be in the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id} and values in the format tagValues/{tag_value_id}.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.servic.description: The service account to be used by the Node VMs. If not specified, the "default" service account is used.
The set of Google API scopes to be made available on all of the node VMs under the service_account specified. These can be either FQDNs, or scope aliases.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.subnet.description: The name or self_link of the Google Compute Engine subnetwork the cluster will be part of. Conflicts with network.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.tags.description: The list of instance tags applied to instances in the cluster. Tags are used to identify valid sources or targets for network firewalls.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.zone.description: The GCP zone where your data is stored and used (i.e. where the master and the worker nodes will be created in). If region is set to 'global' (default) then zone is mandatory, otherwise GCP is able to make use of Auto Zone Placement to determine this automatically for you. Note: This setting additionally determines and restricts which computing resources are available for use with other configs such as cluster_config.master_config.machine_type and cluster_config.worker_config.machine_type.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.confid.description: Confidential Instance Config for clusters using Compute Engine Confidential VMs.
Defines whether the instance should have confidential compute enabled.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.node_g.description: Node Group Affinity for sole-tenant clusters.
The URI of a sole-tenant that the cluster will be created on.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.reserv.description: Reservation Affinity for consuming Zonal reservation.
Corresponds to the label key of reservation resource.
Corresponds to the label values of reservation resource.

cluster_config.gce_cluster_config.shield.description: Shielded Instance Config for clusters using Compute Engine Shielded VMs.
Defines whether instances have integrity monitoring enabled.
Defines whether instances have Secure Boot enabled.
Defines whether instances have the vTPM enabled.

cluster_config.initialization_action.description: Commands to execute on each node after config is completed. You can specify multiple versions of these.

cluster_config.initialization_action.scr.description: The script to be executed during initialization of the cluster. The script must be a GCS file with a gs:// prefix.

cluster_config.initialization_action.tim.description: The maximum duration (in seconds) which script is allowed to take to execute its action. GCP will default to a predetermined computed value if not set (currently 300).

cluster_config.lifecycle_config.description: The settings for auto stop and deletion cluster schedule.

cluster_config.lifecycle_config.auto_del.description: The time when cluster will be auto-deleted. A timestamp in RFC3339 UTC "Zulu" format, accurate to nanoseconds. Example: "2014-10-02T15:01:23.045123456Z".

cluster_config.lifecycle_config.auto_sto.description: The time when cluster will be auto-stopped. A timestamp in RFC3339 UTC "Zulu" format, accurate to nanoseconds. Example: "2014-10-02T15:01:23.045123456Z".

cluster_config.lifecycle_config.idle_del.description: The duration to keep the cluster alive while idling (no jobs running). After this TTL, the cluster will be deleted. Valid range: [300s, 1209600s].

cluster_config.lifecycle_config.idle_sto.description: The duration to keep the cluster started while idling (no jobs running). After this TTL, the cluster will be stopped. Valid range: [10m, 14d].

cluster_config.master_config.description: The Compute Engine config settings for the cluster's master instance.

cluster_config.master_config.image_uri.description: The URI for the image to use for this master

cluster_config.master_config.machine_typ.description: The name of a Google Compute Engine machine type to create for the master

cluster_config.master_config.min_cpu_pla.description: The name of a minimum generation of CPU family for the master. If not specified, GCP will default to a predetermined computed value for each zone.

cluster_config.master_config.num_instanc.description: Specifies the number of master nodes to create. If not specified, GCP will default to a predetermined computed value.

cluster_config.master_config.accelerator.description: The Compute Engine accelerator (GPU) configuration for these instances. Can be specified multiple times.

cluster_config.master_config.instance_fl.description: Instance flexibility Policy allowing a mixture of VM shapes
List of instance selection options that the group will use when creating new VMs.

Preference of this instance selection. Lower number means higher preference. Dataproc will first try to create a VM based on the machine-type with priority rank and fallback to next rank based on availability. Machine types and instance selections with the same priority have the same preference.

cluster_config.metastore_config.dataproc.description: Resource name of an existing Dataproc Metastore service.

cluster_config.preemptible_worker_config.description: The Google Compute Engine config settings for the additional (aka preemptible) instances in a cluster.
Specifies the number of preemptible nodes to create. Defaults to 0.
Specifies the preemptibility of the secondary nodes. Defaults to PREEMPTIBLE.
Indicates how many IOPS to provision for the disk. This sets the number of I/O operations per second that the disk can handle.
Indicates how much throughput to provision for the disk. This sets the number of throughput mb per second that the disk can handle.

Size of the primary disk attached to each preemptible worker node, specified in GB. The smallest allowed disk size is 10GB. GCP will default to a predetermined computed value if not set (currently 500GB). Note: If SSDs are not attached, it also contains the HDFS data blocks and Hadoop working directories.

Interface type of local SSDs (default is "scsi"). Valid values: "scsi" (Small Computer System Interface), "nvme" (Non-Volatile Memory Express).
The amount of local SSD disks that will be attached to each preemptible worker node. Defaults to 0.
Instance flexibility Policy allowing a mixture of VM shapes and provisioning models.
List of instance selection options that the group will use when creating new VMs.

Preference of this instance selection. Lower number means higher preference. Dataproc will first try to create a VM based on the machine-type with priority rank and fallback to next rank based on availability. Machine types and instance selections with the same priority have the same preference.
Defines how Dataproc should create VMs with a mixture of provisioning models.
The base capacity that will always use Standard VMs to avoid risk of more preemption than the minimum capacity you need.
The percentage of target capacity that should use Standard VM. The remaining percentage will use Spot VMs.

cluster_config.security_config.identity_.description: User to service account mappings for multi-tenancy.

The cloud Storage URI of a KMS encrypted file containing the root principal password.
The lifetime of the ticket granting ticket, in hours.

cluster_config.software_config.description: The config settings for software inside the cluster.

cluster_config.software_config.image_ver.description: The Cloud Dataproc image version to use for the cluster - this controls the sets of software versions installed onto the nodes when you create clusters. If not specified, defaults to the latest version.

cluster_config.software_config.optional_.description: The set of optional components to activate on the cluster.

cluster_config.software_config.override_.description: A list of override and additional properties (key/value pairs) used to modify various aspects of the common configuration files used when creating a cluster.

cluster_config.worker_config.machine_typ.description: The name of a Google Compute Engine machine type to create for the master/worker

cluster_config.worker_config.min_cpu_pla.description: The name of a minimum generation of CPU family for the master/worker. If not specified, GCP will default to a predetermined computed value for each zone.

cluster_config.worker_config.min_num_ins.description: The minimum number of primary worker instances to create.

cluster_config.worker_config.num_instanc.description: Specifies the number of worker nodes to create. If not specified, GCP will default to a predetermined computed value.

virtual_cluster_config.description: The virtual cluster config is used when creating a Dataproc cluster that does not directly control the underlying compute resources, for example, when creating a Dataproc-on-GKE cluster. Dataproc may set default values, and values may change when clusters are updated. Exactly one of config or virtualClusterConfig must be specified.

virtual_cluster_config.staging_bucket.description: A Cloud Storage bucket used to stage job dependencies, config files, and job driver console output. If you do not specify a staging bucket, Cloud Dataproc will determine a Cloud Storage location (US, ASIA, or EU) for your cluster's staging bucket according to the Compute Engine zone where your cluster is deployed, and then create and manage this project-level, per-location bucket.

virtual_cluster_config.auxiliary_service.description: Auxiliary services configuration for a Cluster.
The Hive Metastore configuration for this workload.
The Hive Metastore configuration for this workload.
The Spark History Server configuration for the workload.
Resource name of an existing Dataproc Cluster to act as a Spark History Server for the workload.

virtual_cluster_config.kubernetes_cluste.description: The configuration for running the Dataproc cluster on Kubernetes.

A namespace within the Kubernetes cluster to deploy into. If this namespace does not exist, it is created. If it exists, Dataproc verifies that another Dataproc VirtualCluster is not installed into it. If not specified, the name of the Dataproc Cluster is used.
The configuration for running the Dataproc cluster on GKE.

A target GKE cluster to deploy to. It must be in the same project and region as the Dataproc cluster (the GKE cluster can be zonal or regional). Format: 'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/clusters/{cluster_id}'

GKE node pools where workloads will be scheduled. At least one node pool must be assigned the DEFAULT GkeNodePoolTarget.Role. If a GkeNodePoolTarget is not specified, Dataproc constructs a DEFAULT GkeNodePoolTarget.
The target GKE node pool. Format: 'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/clusters/{cluster}/nodePools/{nodePool}'
The roles associated with the GKE node pool.
Input only. The configuration for the GKE node pool.
The list of Compute Engine zones where node pool nodes associated with a Dataproc on GKE virtual cluster will be located.
The autoscaler configuration for this node pool. The autoscaler is enabled only when a valid configuration is present.
The maximum number of nodes in the node pool. Must be >= minNodeCount, and must be > 0.
The minimum number of nodes in the node pool. Must be >= 0 and <= maxNodeCount.
The node pool configuration.
The minimum number of nodes in the node pool. Must be >= 0 and <= maxNodeCount.
The name of a Compute Engine machine type.

Minimum CPU platform to be used by this instance. The instance may be scheduled on the specified or a newer CPU platform. Specify the friendly names of CPU platforms, such as "Intel Haswell" or "Intel Sandy Bridge".

Whether the nodes are created as preemptible VM instances. Preemptible nodes cannot be used in a node pool with the CONTROLLER role or in the DEFAULT node pool if the CONTROLLER role is not assigned (the DEFAULT node pool will assume the CONTROLLER role).
Spot flag for enabling Spot VM, which is a rebrand of the existing preemptible flag.
The software configuration for this Dataproc cluster running on Kubernetes.
The components that should be installed in this Dataproc cluster. The key must be a string from the KubernetesComponent enumeration. The value is the version of the software to be installed.
The properties to set on daemon config files. Property keys are specified in prefix:property format, for example spark:spark.kubernetes.container.image.
